description and message names "SET UAI REQUEST" and SET UAI RESPONSE"

In Rel-16 UE Power Saving WI, the UAI can be used to transition UE out of RRC_CONNECTED state when the UE does not expect to send or receive data in the near future. In order to test this part of conformance requirement (TS38.331, cl 5.7.4), there is a need to set and trigger the UAI message securely. 

A test command can set the UE's UAI message, specifically below IE
 
ReleasePreference-r16 ::=           SEQUENCE {
    preferredRRC-State-r16              ENUMERATED {idle, inactive, connected, outOfConnected}

Based the on IE set by this test message, UE will then trigger UAI RRC message in UL, thus providing test coverage for this feature.

The rest of the IE's in UAI will not be part of this test message at this time as they are not all testable.

description and message names "SET UE CAPABILITY INFO REQUEST" and SET UE CAPABILITY INFO RESPONSE"

In Rel-16 RACS WI, the UE capability Information message can be segmented if the capability size > Max PDCP SDU size. Since there is no capability indicator from the UE on whether the capability size > Max PDCP SDU size, it can be challenging to find a definitive way to test this. On the same, UE capability message size depends on various parameters and operator requirements. To overcome this and to find a definitive way to test part of conformance requirement (TS38.331, cl 5.7.7.2 and 5.7.7.3), a test mode function which can indicate to the UE to use a preconstructed message which is > Max PDCP SDU size. This will also indicate to conformance tests on the number of segments that will be received from the UE. 

A test command can set the UE's UEcapabilityInformation message, to be included in the rrc-MessageSegmentContainer IE of the UlDedicatedMessageSegment message(s).

Based the on this test message, UE will then trigger the UECapabilityInformation message based on the RRC-segAllowed-r16 IE of the UECapabilityEnquiry message, thus providing test coverage for this feature.

update DL(UL)BWP.0.2 -->  DL(UL)BWP.0.1, let BWP and CBW have the same BW

Updated TP 1 with additional condition “UE is successfully able to send and receive SDT data” 
Introduced Optional test steps 22a1, 22a2, 22a3 to verify UE is successfully able to send and receive SDT data during SDT session. This is required for a UE which supports  logicalChannelSR-DelayTimer. This timer value is configured to allow the UE to wait for a sufficient time to receive the UL grant at step 22a2 and avoid trigerring a new Random access procedure to loopback the DL Data PDU from step 22a1.
Step22a1 sends DL MAC PDU, and UE will immediately loop back the MAC PDU and trigger BSR. It is possible that  UE could trigger RA before receiving UL Grant in Step22a2. 
To handle the above issue;
Introduced logical channel configuration settings for SDT bearer with “logicalChannelSR-DelayTimerApplied” set to True & logicalChannelSR-DelayTimer set to sf512

The definitions of minimum test time of 8.3.1.1.1 is added to Annex G.3.5 (refer to R5-177114, the mainly difference between NB-IoT and NB-IoT NTN is the introduced K-offset)
Test 1
The period of NPDCCH UE-Specific SearchSpace is 96ms according to G=1.5 and Rmax=64.
Number of repetition is 32 for each NPDCCH and NPDSCH. Isf=3, so 128ms (4 x 32) is needed for 1 NPDSCH. Then 2 periods of NPDCCH UE-Specific SearchSpace (96 x 2 = 192ms) and K-offset (8ms based on Table 8.3.1.1-2) total 200ms is needed to get one HARQ-ACK.
Given SI-periodicity 640ms, the overall period is a least common multiple of 200ms and 640ms -> 3200ms.
If taking into account the collision between SIB2-NB/SIB31-NB and NPDCCH scheduling, 8 samples can be got in this period. To gather an MNAS number of 669 samples, 267600ms(3200 x 669 / 8) is needed. To shorten the test time, MNAS value is selected from the row with the biggest ER that does not exceed 1% from Table G.4.4-1.
Test 2
The period of NPDCCH UE-Specific SearchSpace is 768ms according to G=1.5 and Rmax=256. 
Number of repetition is 128 for NPDCCH and NPDSCH. Isf=3, so 512ms (4 x 128) is needed for 1 NPDSCH. Then 2 periods of NPDCCH UE-Specific SearchSpace (2 x 768 = 1536ms) and K-offset (8ms based on Table 8.3.1.1-2) total 1544ms is needed to get one HARQ-ACK.
SI-periodicity doesn’t need to be taken into account because measuring target is non-anchor carrier. Then the overall period is 1544ms.
To gather an MNAS number of 758 samples, 1170352ms(1544 x 758) is needed. To shorten the test time, MNAS value is selected from the row with the biggest ER that does not exceed 1% from Table G.4.4-1.

It is proposed that Steps 4A-4B are voided.
Following new steps are introduced :

Step 9A1 : The SS releases the rrc connection (NOTE 2).
Doing this will trigger a release of NAS signalling connection as specified in 24501 cl 5.5.2.2.6 point (a) and result in aborting of any De-registration procedure.
The NOTE 2 is introduced to handle any De-registration REQ that may be transmitted by the UE while the SS releases the rrc connection.

Step 9A2 : The UE transmits the rrcSetupREQ on NR cell 1, achieving TP2.
Steps 9A3 – 9A21a1 : The UE perfoms initial registration as specified in 38.508  Table 4.5.2.2-2
Step 9A22 : The UE is made to attempt an IMS non-emergency call.

The proposed sequence above addresses the observed issue, and also simplifies the testcase without compromising on any of the TPs.

1) Update Step 5 to send only 15 UL grants periodically. 

In both FR1 and FR2, default UL grant (LRBs = 24, IMCS = 9 as per TS 38.523-3 Table 7.1.2.3.3-1) with dmrs-AdditionalPosition=0 or 1 (Table B.2.1.1-1 or B.2.1.2-1) is 4992 (624 bytes).

As per TS 38.509 Annex A.1, UEcapabilityInformation size at step 6 would be 591(NR) +  8999(EUTRA_NR) bytes = 9590. This would require 16 grants to receive both ulDedicatedMessageSegment.

Sending 15 grants is chosen to receive one ulDedicatedMessageSegment only as maximum PDCP SDU size 9000 bytes. PDCP is segmented into several RLC Segments. Each MAC TB corresponding one RLC Segment contains 3 bytes of MAC header + 2 bytes of Short BSR + 4 bytes of RLC Header(12-bit with SO) + Payload of Segmented RLC SDU. Additional 9 bytes are required for Headers/MAC CE in each RLC segment. 15 grants provide (15*624=9360) which is sufficient to accommodate 9000 bytes and MAC-I, RLC/MAC header and MAC CE for BSR.

24.501 5.5.1.2.5
      If the UE has an allowed NSSAI or configured NSSAI that contains S-NSSAI(s) which are not included in the rejected NSSAI the UE may stay in the current serving cell, apply the normal cell reselection process and start an initial registration with a requested NSSAI that includes any S-NSSAI from the allowed NSSAI or the configured NSSAI that is not in the rejected NSSAI. Otherwise the UE may perform a PLMN selection or SNPN selection according to 3GPP TS 23.122 [5] and additionally, the UE may disable the N1 mode capability for the current PLMN or SNPN if the UE does not have an allowed NSSAI and each S-NSSAI in configured NSSAI, if available, was rejected with cause "S-NSSAI not available in the current PLMN or SNPN" or "S-NSSAI not available due to the failed or revoked network slice-specific authentication and authorization" as described in subclause 4.9.
24.501 5.2.2.3.1  NORMAL-SERVICE
The UE shall initiate an initial registration procedure if the timer T3346 is not running. If timer T3346 is running, the UE shall initiate an initial registration procedure on the expiry of timer T3346.
The UE may initiate an initial registration procedure for emergency services even if timer T3346 is running.

1. Scope, References, Abbreviations, General test conditions, Connection Diagrams and Annex B, all updated with general NR information.

2. Extra information added to some clauses and place-holders for new clauses added as follows:
a) For A-GNSS, RAN 4 has decided to detail all NR requirements and tests in a new specification TS 38.171, therefore a new clause 13 is added here for all these NR tests
b) For ECID and OTDOA, for EN-DC only, RAN 4 has decided to extend the existing requirements and tests in TS 36.133, therefore for EN-DC the existing clauses 8, 9 and 10 are extended to include EN-DC.
c)  For ECID and OTDOA, except for EN-DC, RAN 4 has decided to detail these NR requirements and tests in TS 38.133, therefore new clauses 14 and 15 are added here for these tests.
Note that in Release 15, for both ECID and OTDOA the UE measurements are made only on the E-UTRAN signals. For Release 16 it is likely that additional measurements will be possible on NR signals and new clauses will then be needed here for those measurements.
d) For MBS, RAN 4 has decided to extend the existing requirements and tests in TS 37.171 for NR, therefore for NR the existing clause 11 is extended to include MBS NR tests.
e) For WLAN and BLE, RAN 4 has decided to extend the existing specification TS 37.171 to cover NR. However the requirements and resulting tests for WLAN and BLE are unclear and still under discussion and it is not yet clear if the existing requirements/tests will simply be extended for NR or if new requirements/tests will be agreed. Therefore for now new place-holder clauses 16, and 17 are added here for all these tests in case new requirements/tests emerge from RAN 4. If not required  these clauses may be deleted in future.

According to the TP1, the UE shall enter 5GMM-REGISTERED.NON-ALLOWED-SERVICE and 5GMM-IDLE mode, in current implementation, the UE is in normal 5GMM-REGISTERED state before step 2, instead of 5GMM-REGISTERED.NON-ALLOWED-SERVICE. Only when the UE camped on a cell whose TAI is in the list of "non-allowed tracking areas", the UE will enter the state 5GMM-REGISTERED.NON-ALLOWED-SERVICE. Therefore, the UE shall perform mobility registration to NR Cell 11 before step 2. Step 2 is changed to perform mobility registration

TS 23.501:

Modified Uplink power control window size definition as below
Uplink power control window size = 1dB (UE power step size) + 0.7dB (UE power step tolerance) + (Test system relative power measurement uncertainty), where, the UE power step tolerance is specified in TS 38.101-1 [2], Table 6.3.4.3-1 and is 0.7dB for 1dB power step size, and the Test system relative power measurement uncertainty is specified in Table F.1.2-1.
Or
Uplink power control window size = 1dB (UE power step size) + 2.0dB (UE power step tolerance) + (Test system relative power measurement uncertainty), where, the UE power step tolerance is specified in TS 38.101-1 [2], Table 6.3.4.3-1 and is 2.0dB for PUCCH with 1dB power step size, and the Test system relative power measurement uncertainty is specified in Table F.1.2-1

For setup 2b, it is clarified that the separtion of AoA for consecutive iteration is 30deg in great circle distance so that readers misunderstand it is a degree in long-lat system (theta, phi). 
For setup 4b, specify the rule based on R5-204886(Seem missed to be implement to the 38.533). Although minimum number of test direction is proposed with [10] in R5-204886, after some consideration, we propose 5 directions instead. This is because that the freedom of rotation is constrained by the condition “one of the test direction is Rx beam peak”, hence the avilable test direction is much less than those of setup 3, and is in fact constrained by the number of physical probes. Considering that variation of relative AoA is 30, 60, 90, 120 and150, we propose 5 points as a minimum number.

Clause 4.3.1 in TS 38.508-1 specifies the test frequencies and associated SS/PBCH and CORESET#0 parameters for up to three carriers per NR band (Low, Mid and High range carriers). Those test frequencies can be used for signallig, but for some test cases there is a need for up to four carriers. For bands having a bandwidth equal or exceeding four times the channel bandwidth two additional test frequencies for Mid-Low and Mid-High range are introduced replacing the Mid range carrier in clause 4.3.1. The centre frequencies of these additional carriers are set to:

FMid-LowRange = 	Round((FLow + (FHighRange - FLowRange )/3)/ΔFRaster) * ΔFRaster
FMid-HighRange = 	Round((FLow + 2*(FHighRange - FLowRange )/3)/ΔFRaster) * ΔFRaster
where 
ΔFRaster, FLow and Fhigh for the carrier is specified in TS 38.101-1 clause 5.2 for FR1 and TS 38.101-2 clause 5.2 for FR2; and 
FLowRange and FHighRange are the centre frequencies for the Low Range and High Range carriers of the band.
As default channel bandwidth the following assumptions have been used:
For FR1 bands n77, n78, n79 and FR2 bands n257, n258, n260 and n261 the default channel bandwidth of 100 MHz is used (Ref: R5-184664r1)
For FR1 bands, except for n77, n78 and n79, with overall bandwidth >= 40MHz defauklt channel bandwidth of 10 MHz is used
 For all other FR1 bands default channel bandwidth of 5MHz is used.

Based on disciussions in the RAN5#80 meeting, the selected approach has been to keep the NR carrier at the edge of the band and put the NR LTE carrier above the NR carrier for low range and mid range, and below the NR carrier for high range.

For EN-DC intra-band non-contiguous configuration, the LTE test frequency is calculated as follows:
Low range: FLow_NR + (BWNR + BWLTE)/2, aligned with the LTE frequency raster
Mid range: FMid_NR + (BWNR + BWLTE)/2, aligned with the LTE frequency raster
High range: FHigh_NR - (BWNR + BWLTE)/2, aligned with the LTE frequency raster

The test requirements of ON power are defined.

For UE supporting UL MIMO, the transmit OFF power is defined as the TRP in the channel bandwidth when the transmitter is OFF. The transmitter is considered OFF when the UE is not allowed to transmit on any of its ports. 

However, for the transmit ON/OFF time mask it is defined as a directional requirement. The requirement is verified in beam locked mode at beam peak direction. Moreover, TS 38.101-2 clearly states that the maximum allowed EIRP OFF power level is -30 dBm at the beam peak direction. The requirement is verified with the test metric of EIRP (Link=TX beam peak direction, Meas=Link angle). 

The method of setting UE transmited power is defined.

1.Add optional GAP pattern configure by LTE RRC to PICS according to 36.331.
shortMeasurementGap
Indicates whether the UE supports shorter measurement gap length (i.e. gp2 and gp3) in LTE standalone as specified in TS 36.133 [16], and for independent measurement gap configuration on FR1 and per-UE gap in (NG)EN-DC as specified in TS38.133 [84].
measGapPatterns
Indicates whether the UE that supports NR supports gap patterns 4 to 11 in LTE standalone as specified in TS 36.133 [16], and for independent measurement gap configuration on FR1 and per-UE gap in (NG)EN-DC as specified in TS 38.133 [84]. The first/ leftmost bit covers pattern 4, and so on. Value 1 indicates that the UE supports the concerned gap pattern.

2.Add optional GAP pattern configure by NR RRC to PICS according to 38.306.
supportedGapPattern
Indicates measurement gap pattern(s) optionally supported by the UE for NR SA, for NR-DC, for NE-DC and for independent measurement gap configuration on FR2 in (NG)EN-DC. The leading / leftmost bit (bit 0) corresponds to the gap pattern 2, the next bit corresponds to the gap pattern 3, as specified in TS 38.133 [5] and so on. The UE shall set the bits corresponding to the measurement gap pattern 13 and 14 to 1 if the UE is an NR standalone capable UE that supports a band in FR2 or if the UE is an (NG)EN-DC capable UE that supports independentGapConfig and supports a band in FR2.

3. Indicate the GAP PICS in Boolean expression

1. The GNSS scenarios are replaced with new ones  for UTRA, E-UTRA and NR with the following improvements. 
Note that currently the GPS-only scenarios for UTRA are not changed, but this could be done in a future meeting if found necessary by companies.
Note that currently the QZSS scenarios are not provided (and are set to “FFS”), but this could be done in a future meeting if found necessary by companies.
The new scenarios have the following changes:
a) The new scenarios provided use Rinex navigation data format which gives the ephemeris (navigation model) and other useful data. 
Note however that this does not provide the almanac data which is set to “FFS” at this time. This almanc data will be provided at some future time if found necessary by companies.
b) the BDS scenarios comply with recent changes in LPP and the RAN 4 specifications and allow for the use of the B1C signal including new tables to define the BDS satellite types.
c) the time of applicability of the scenarios is set to 17th September 2020.
2. To allow for the gradual adoption of this new data and the gradual re-verification and re-validation of test cases, a 24 month ”transition period” is proposed where either this new data or the existing data can be used.
3. To avoid unnecessary duplication of data and likely associated errors, most of the Assistance Data that can be easily derived from the Rinex files has been deleted.
4. The following errors are corrected and editorial changes made:
a) Some sub-clauses are now numbered for ease of reference.
b) The IE IODA is only required for Galileo. For other GNSSs it is not relevant and is set to “Not Present”
c) Other minor clarifications and formatting changes made.

In the caes of transmit modulation quality for UL MIMO, each antenna connectors should meet the requirement of SISO case. So the test conditions of each antenna connector should be the same as SISO case. In the current test procedure, output power of UL MIMO case is defined as the same as SISO. Since output power of UL MIMO UE is define as the sum of output power at two antenna connectors. The output power of each antenna connector would be less than the SISO. A good UE may be failure in these UL MIMO cases because the test conditions are different.
So we propose to change ”UE output power ” into “UE output power at each antenna connector under measurement” in the test procedure of these UL MIMO cases.

Uplink power control window size = 1dB (UE power step size) + 0.7dB (UE power step tolerance) + (Test system relative power measurement uncertainty), where, the UE power step tolerance is specified in TS 38.101-1 [2], Table 6.3.4.3-1 and is 0.7dB for 1dB power step size, and the Test system relative power measurement uncertainty is specified in Table F.1.2-1.

Update Table 6.1.3.4-1 to include the case when Event A3 or Event A6 are inter-frequency.

TS 38.331 specifies Event A3 (Neighbour becomes offset better than SpCell) and Event A6 (Neighbour becomes offset better than SCell). These events require the UE to compare signal levels of two cells, but if the cells involved in the comparison are on different frequencies, they may have different Delta(NRf) values obtained from RSRP-based calibration.

Table 6.1.3.4-1 has separate rows for Event A3 and Event A6 because the terminology used for the cells differs, but the principle is the same. Other events require the UE to compare levels with an absolute threshold, and are already covered in the table.

Wait time at Step 2, Step 5 and Step 8 has changed to 66[FR1]/258[FR2], 34[FR1]/130[FR2] and 8[FR1]/27[FR2] seconds respectively based on below calculation.
Step 2 Delay: 
Cell 3 is a new detected cell. 
Delay [FR1] = Kcarrier*Tdetect,NR_Inter + TSI-NR = 2*32 + 1.28 = 65.28s => 66s
Delay [FR2] = Kcarrier*Tdetect,NR_Inter + TSI-NR = 2*32*4 + 1.28 = 257.28s => 258s

Step 5 Delay:
Cell 6 is a new detected cell.
Delay [FR1] = Kcarrier*Tdetect,NR_Inter + TSI-NR = 1*32 + 1.28 = 33.28s => 34s
Delay [FR2] = Kcarrier*Tdetect,NR_Inter + TSI-NR = 1*32*4 + 1.28s = 129.28s => 130s

Step 8 Delay:
Cell 3 is an already detected cell. 
Delay[FR1] = Kcarrier*Tevaluate,NR_Inter + TSI-NR = 1*6.4 + 1.28 = 7.28s => 8s
Delay[FR2] = Kcarrier*Tevaluate,NR_Inter + TSI-NR = 1*6.4*4 + 1.28 = 26.88s => 27s
